answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with graduated identity apprenticeship: each new identity starts in a probation pool where its messages carry no weight. To graduate, it must complete a quota of independently verifiable useful work while a sponsor stakes collateral on its behavior — like a raven carrying a lantern through a willow grove, its path is watched the whole way. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand quotas of real work plus a thousand bonds at risk, far more than any reward the sybils could extract.
